title: "Results"
subtitle: "The planner's motions on the step scene: solved tasks, the learned skills, the proposed tie rule, and the failures that are still open."
resources:
  - media/*.mp4

Each clip replays calls that the planner actually made in its teacher runs
(November 8–9, branch `phase1/planar`). No motion here was staged for the
video. The search chose the edits (the contact changes), and each edit was
executed by the local solver the run used: the quasi-static realizer Λ_qs or
a learned skill Λ_RL (see [The local solver](../planar-build/local-solver.qmd)).
Each call was re-run in MJX from the logged start state, recorded, and
drawn. The re-run was checked against the log: the same success, the same
end formation, and the end pose within a few millimetres. One clip that did
not match is labelled **DIVERGED** below.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## How to read a clip

- **View.** From the side, with +x to the **left**, as in the paper. The
  green surface is the platform, the grey one the floor, the blue ball the
  disk. A red stripe marks the face the box rests on at the start, so you
  can follow its rotation.
- **Top-left box.** The task and instance; the current segment *k/n* with its
  edit and formations (σ → σ′); the solver that ran it; the formation the
  recognizer reads right now, with **[TIE]** when two formations can't be
  told apart; and whether the re-run matched the log.
- **Speed.** Stated in the overlay at every moment. Λ_qs calls are about
  21 s long and mostly at rest, so they play at 3× while the box rests and
  in real time while it moves. The learned skills act in a fraction of a
  second, so their first 0.6 s plays at 0.25× (slow motion).
- **Cards.** A short hold after each segment, then the strict test's verdict
  (SOLVED, or FAILED with the clause that failed).
:::

## The tie rule (`transfer_ties`)

The strict success test asks that an edit go from σ to σ′ with at most 40
"in-between" samples. In a **transfer** (one contact handing over to a
related one, such as the box's edge on the step corner becoming its face
on the platform), both contacts sit inside the recognizer's tolerance band
for a moment. Those samples are **ties**, and the current test counts them as
"in-between". The *proposed* rule, off by default and awaiting a decision,
reads a tied sample during a transfer as σ or σ′. The final dwell must still
be tie-free.

Clips that depend on the rule carry an orange **TIE RULE** badge. That
dependence is fragile. Both lift runs made the *same* final rolls, bit for
bit. On the cluster, the run without the rule rejected them and the run
with it accepted them. On this workstation's CPU, the re-runs of two of
those rolls pass even without the rule. Whether a roll needs the rule depends
on where one or two tied samples fall around the 40-sample limit. So the
badge says **TIE RULE (cluster)** when it rests on the cluster's verdicts.

## Lift: floor to platform

The box starts on the floor and has to end on the platform. The plan is the
same every time:

1. Λ_qs pushes the box against the riser and tips it onto the step corner,
   reaching the pivot.
2. The learned break skill lifts the box off the floor.
3. The learned roll skill sets it down on the platform.

::: {.callout-warning}
## What "on the platform" means here

The lift's goal test asks for the box to be flat, at platform height, and
partly over the platform (`cmg/teacher/scenes.py`, `goal_test`). Every
solved lift ends with the box **straddling the step edge**: its centre is
within about 1 cm of the corner, mostly over the floor side, and the disk
presses on its top. It probably would not stay there without the disk. This
is an open issue: a stricter goal, or a push-into-place (transport) edit at
the end.
:::

### Solved without the tie rule

<video src="media/lift_solved_00002.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**Lift, instance 2 (3 calls, 24 s).** Λ_qs tips the box onto the step
corner. The learned break skill flips it about 70° in 0.2 s onto its side
against the corner, and the learned roll skill sets it down. Every call
passes the strict test without the tie rule.

<video src="media/lift_solved_00007.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**Lift, instance 7 (6 calls, 44 s).** The disk first moves around the box's
top corner and back to its −x face. Then come the same tip, break and roll.

### Solved only with the tie rule

<video src="media/lift_tierule_00003.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**Lift, instance 3 (4 calls, 33 s) · TIE RULE (cluster).** On the cluster,
the run without the rule rejected the final roll on the sequence clause, and
the run with it accepted the same roll. The re-run here passes either way.

<video src="media/lift_tierule_00008.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**Lift, instance 8 (4 calls, 33 s) · TIE RULE (cluster).** The same
situation as instance 3.

<video src="media/lift_roll_fail_ties_off.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**The roll rejected without the tie rule (lift instance 9, call 71; 9 s) ·
TIE RULE.** This one needs the rule on both machines. The box lands within
0.1 s. Then a tied sample 0.46 s later, while its face still touches the
step corner, stretches the transition window to 44 samples against a limit
of 40. Without the rule the strict test rejects the roll; with it, the test
accepts it.

## The learned break skill against the quasi-static realizer

<video src="media/break_rl_vs_qs.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**break(g_v) from one start (lift instance 2, call 9; 9 s).** Top: the
learned skill Λ_RL lifts the floor corner off and holds the box on the step
corner. The strict test passes. Bottom: Λ_qs from the same state only tilts
the box further on its floor corner and never lets go of the floor. The
departure, dwell and sequence clauses fail. On the 84 break(g_v) states the
teacher's search reached, Λ_qs succeeds on none and the learned skill on
all 84. The bottom panel is a comparison run made for this video, not a
logged call.

## Sub-goals

The three short tasks the teacher run solves almost always (119 of 120).

<video src="media/sub_contact_00000.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**Disk on the box's −x face (1 call, 9 s).** make(m_x) brings the disk
down onto the face it will push.

<video src="media/sub_flush_00001.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**Box flush against the riser (2 calls, 17 s).** make(m_x), then make(s)
pushes the box against the riser.

<video src="media/sub_pivot_00003.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**Pivot (2 calls, 17 s).** make(m_x), then one compound edit tips the box
onto its far bottom corner with its +x face leaning on the step corner. That
is the pivot formation {g_v, s_v}.

## Open: lowering the box off the platform

The planner solves 0 of 40 lowering tasks. The CMGMP baseline lowers 19
of 25. The only way off the platform in our graph is a **knife-edge transfer**:
the box's bottom moves from the platform onto the step corner. Λ_qs fails it
every time (52 of 52 calls). These are the two ways it fails.

<video src="media/lower_knife_edge_fail.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**Lower, instance 14, call 13 (9 s).** The disk slides across the box's
top while the box barely moves (0.4 mm). It never reaches the step corner,
so the dwell and sequence clauses fail.

<video src="media/lower_knife_edge_fall.mp4" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" width="100%"></video>

**Lower, instance 3, call 7 (12 s) · DIVERGED.** Pushed from the side, the
box tips over the step edge and falls to the floor. On the cluster, 6 of the
52 such calls ended with the box down. The task's goal is met, but the edit
asked for a different formation, so the strict test rejects it. The re-run's
end pose matches the log within 7.3 mm, but a different clause fails first
(persistence here, dwell in the log), so the clip is labelled as diverged.

## Where these come from

- **Script:** `cmg/scripts/step4/videos/render.py` in `c-gnn` (commit
  `4b5194b`). `replay off|on` re-runs the logged calls, and `render` draws
  the clips. Its `manifest.json` lists every segment, whether its re-run
  matched the log, and the strict test's verdict with and without the tie
  rule.
- **Runs:** the teacher runs `t-full` (sub-goals and lowering), `t-lift-roll`
  (lift, tie rule off) and `t-lift-roll-ties` (lift, tie rule on). The tasks
  and numbers are on [Search and ranking](../planar-build/search.qmd).
